newsitem.title: GREECE: MORE TESTIFY IN GREECE'S DELTA BOURSE SCANDAL.
newsitem.headline: MORE TESTIFY IN GREECE'S DELTA BOURSE SCANDAL.

text.p: Investigating magistrate Costas Ganiatsos heard more testimony in the Delta settlement scandal which stopped trading at the bourse and he will visit the stock exchange on Friday, court sources said.

Ganiatsos heard testimony from Panagiotis Kondalexis,the president of the Association of Athens Stock Exchange Members (SMEHA), from reporter Andonis Pikoulas of Kathimerini newspaper and former Delta client Spyros Giasafakis, sources told Reuters.
He will not hear testimony on Friday because of a visit to the stock exchange, the sources said.
Spyros Giasafakis, a paint merchant and Delta Securities client, has sued Delta for forgery, fraud and defamation, the sources said.
Giasafakis says he made two trades with Delta amounting to 8.0 million drachmas.
He is suing the brokerage because it shows him as the client behind trades worth 1.5 billion drachmas on November 7, one day before the scandal broke at the clearing house, court sources said.
Two more individuals are shown by Delta to have traded large amounts but their identities were not available, court sources said.
Delta failed to meet settlement payments of 2.6 billion drachmas, triggering the crisis which effectively closed the bourse for four days.
SMEHA has asked that bourse authorities and the government impose tighter regulatory controls on the clearing house and on transactions by brokers.

Delta has been charged with "large-scale and repeated" fraud and the public prosecutor has also laid charges against unnamed persons at the bourse. --George Georgiopoulos, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
